title: Connectivity Guardrails: Audit Schema, SIEM Export, and Network Hardening Checklist
body:
Purpose:
Ensure private deployments have a concise, operationally-actionable reference for network-level guardrails: VPC topology patterns, firewall rule templates, mTLS terminologies and placement, RBAC v2 audit bindings, an audit-log schema for SIEM ingestion, and an evidence automation runbook for compliance reviews. This doc is intended for infra engineers who onboard customers to Private and SRE/Trust teams doing evidence collection.

Scope and intent:
- Scope: customer-managed VPCs and Redwood-managed private control plane connectivity (VPC peering, PrivateLink/endpoint services, transit/hub patterns).
- Intent: minimize blast radius, provide deterministic evidence output for audit, and keep operational paths (failopen/fallback) explicit.

High-level network patterns (recommendations):
1) Minimal-acceptance hub-spoke (recommended for enterprise customers):
   - Hub (shared services): centralized NGFW, SIEM forwarder, and NAT - placed in shared-services subnet in hosting account.
   - Spokes: each customer deployment runs in isolated spoke VPCs with explicit route propagation to hub.
   - Control plane connectivity: private endpoint (PrivateLink) from customer VPC to Redwood control plane in Redwood account - strongly preferred over cross-account NAT.

2) Customer-managed firewall edge with Redwood ingress endpoints:
   - Keep ingress (public) endpoints in a dedicated perimeter subnet that terminates TLS only at the customer edge (if required by policy).
   - When customer requests Redwood-managed TLS termination, mTLS must be enforced to a customer-facing edge proxy with a documented certificate chain.

3) Transit gateway for multi-region workloads:
   - Use TGW or cloud equivalent; restrict route tables so only monitoring and SIEM egress flows cross the transit.

mTLS placement and topology guidance:
- Mode A: End-to-end mTLS (preferred): client -> customer edge proxy -> Redwood runtime -> Redwood control plane; mutual TLS enforced at every hop. Keys stored in customer KMS/HSM where required.
- Mode B: mTLS at perimeter only: customer client <-> customer edge mTLS; internal traffic authenticated via short-lived tokens (use when customer cannot provide certs).
- Termination rules: Redwood will not terminate customer private keys. If Redwood manages TLS, we require a documented key escrow and rotation policy and customer approval.

Firewall rule templates (cloud-generic examples - convert to provider syntax as needed):
- Ingress to runtime subnet: allow tcp 443 from customer-edge-proxy-cidrs; deny 0.0.0.0/0 unless explicitly required.
- Egress to control plane: allow tcp 443 to redwood-control-plane-ips; restrict to specific ports for metrics/health/management.
- SIEM forwarder: allow udp 514/tcp 514 (syslog) or HTTPS 443 to SIEM collector IPs; prefer TLS with mTLS when supported.
- Admin jump host: allow ssh 22 from audited-bastion-cidrs only; require MFA and ephemeral certs.

Example iptables-like rule set (for on-prem integrations):
- allow INPUT tcp --dport 443 -s 10.100.0.0/22 -m comment --comment "customer-edge" -j ACCEPT
- allow OUTPUT tcp --dport 9200 -d 10.200.10.5/32 -m comment --comment "siem-elastic" -j ACCEPT
- drop INPUT all -s 0.0.0.0/0 -m comment --comment "default deny" -j DROP

RBAC v2 mapping (network and audit perspective):
- Roles (examples): network-reader, network-admin, evidence-collector, control-plane-operator.
- Resource patterns: "resource:private:vpc:{customer_id}:{vpc_id}" and "resource:private:runtime:{customer_id}:{runtime_id}".
- Attribute-based policy suggestions: allow network-admin to modify security-groups only when request includes justification tag and requestor has "change-control" entitlement.

Audit log schema (single-event schema for SIEM ingestion):
- event_time: RFC3339 timestamp
- event_id: UUIDv4
- source: enum ["vpc-flow", "firewall", "mtls", "rbac", "evidence-automation"]
- resource: string (resource pattern described above)
- src_ip: string
- dst_ip: string
- src_port: number
- dst_port: number
- action: enum ["ALLOW", "DENY", "REJECT"]
- verdict: enum ["success", "fail", "partial"]
- user: string (identity principal e.g., svc-account:infra-deployer or user:elena.petrov@redwood.com)
- role: string (RBAC role at the time of event)
- request_id: opaque id tying logs to telemetry/traces
- trace_id: optional trace id
- details: freeform message
- evidence_refs: list (comma-separated strings) pointing to archived evidence blobs (e.g., s3://redwood-evidence/PD-742/2026-02-12/packet-capture.pcap)

Sample audit event (as an embedded line - this must be ingested as JSON by SIEM):
{
  "event_time": "2026-02-12T14:22:35Z",
  "event_id": "d2f1c6a6-6c2b-4e9f-9f3c-2a7f6b1e9fa2",
  "source": "firewall",
  "resource": "resource:private:vpc:acme-inc:vpc-0a1b2c3d",
  "src_ip": "34.120.12.45",
  "dst_ip": "10.10.5.12",
  "src_port": 54822,
  "dst_port": 443,
  "action": "DENY",
  "verdict": "fail",
  "user": "svc-account:fw-collector",
  "role": "network-reader",
  "request_id": "req-8a7d3f",
  "trace_id": "4d5f6e7a",
  "details": "blocked unexpected source to runtime endpoint",
  "evidence_refs": "s3://evidence/acme/PD-742/2026-02-12/fw-log-14-22.json"
}

SIEM export mapping (fields -> SIEM destination keys):
- event_time -> @timestamp (Elasticsearch) or _time (Splunk)
- event_id -> event.id
- source -> event.module
- resource -> host.identifier or asset.id
- src_ip/dst_ip -> source.ip / destination.ip
- user -> user.name
- role -> user.role
- evidence_refs -> related.evidence (array of URLs)

Transport considerations for SIEM:
- Preferred: encrypted HTTPS webhook with mTLS (collector <-> SIEM) and JSON Lines payloads.
- Backup: batched S3 export with signed URLs; collector writes compressed daily bundles and atomically uploads.

Evidence automation runbook (quick steps to generate audit artefacts for compliance):
1) Trigger: scheduled daily / on-demand (sensitivity: pre-audit).
2) Collectors: firewall logs, VPC flow logs, mTLS session summaries, RBAC change events, runtime health checks.
3) Normalize: run normalization lambda to output our audit schema (see above).
4) Store: upload normalized JSON lines to customer evidence bucket with path: s3://redwood-evidence/{customer}/{audit_date}/{artifact}.json.gz.
5) Hash & sign: compute SHA256 and sign with automation-signer key; store hashes in index file.
6) Index: push a small index doc to the control-plane metadata DB for quick lookups (index contains event ranges and file refs).
7) Retention & purge: default 365d (configurable per contract).

Automation snippets (pseudo commands):
- collect-firewall-logs --since "24h" --out /tmp/fw.jsonl
- normalize-to-audit --in /tmp/fw.jsonl --schema audit_v1 --out /tmp/fw-audit.jsonl
- aws s3 cp /tmp/fw-audit.jsonl.gz s3://redwood-evidence/acme/2026-02-12/fw-audit.jsonl.gz --acl bucket-owner-full-control

Hardening checklist (operational tasks):
- [ ] Confirm PrivateLink endpoints exist and are restricted to expected subnets.
- [ ] Verify security groups follow least privilege; no wide-open 0.0.0.0/0 where not required.
- [ ] Ensure mTLS is configured between edge proxy and Redwood runtime where policy requires it.
- [ ] Validate RBAC v2 bindings: evidence-collector role scoped to read-only for logs only.
- [ ] Confirm SIEM forwarder uses mTLS or signed HTTPS with rotated certs.
- [ ] Run automated evidence collector and validate index contains today's files.
- [ ] Review firewall deny counters and escalate spikes > 5x baseline.
- [ ] Confirm key rotation policy documented and GCP/AWS KMS rotation enabled where used.

Operational run scenarios (short):
- Scenario A (packet capture request during compliance review): run collector, produce pcap.gz, upload to evidence bucket, link event IDs in audit logs.
- Scenario B (RBAC change): any RBAC role change triggers an audit event; automation collects before/after bindings and uploads for review.

Troubleshooting notes (common issues):
- Missing flow logs: check VPC flow logging state, S3/GCS sink permissions, and retention lifecycle.
- SIEM ingestion backpressure: fallback to S3 export; alert on collector queue growth > 10k events/min.

Appendix A — ASCII diagram (simplified):

  +-----------------+      PrivateLink/API      +------------------------+
  | customer edge   |-------------------------->| redwood control plane  |
  | proxy (mTLS)    |                           | (private endpoints)    |
  +--------+--------+                           +-----------+------------+
           |                                                 |
           |   Hub (shared services)                         |
           |   NGFW / SIEM forwarder                         |
           v                                                 v
  +-----------------+                                  +-----------------+
  | customer VPC    | <--- spoke -- transit -- spoke -->| runtime VPC     |
  | (apps)          |                                  | (redwood runtime)|
  +-----------------+                                  +-----------------+

Appendix B — sample queries (for SOC):
- Splunk: index=redwood_fw source=firewall action=DENY | stats count by src_ip, dst_ip | sort -count
- ES/Kibana: POST /_search { "query": { "term": { "action": "DENY" } } }

Open questions / decisions required:
- Define SLA for evidence delivery for enterprise audits (current default: within 4 hours of on-demand request).
- Customer key-holding model vs Redwood-managed short-lived certs: finalize default for regulated customers.

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc draws from multiple previous playbooks but intentionally reorganizes around the audit schema + SIEM export concern. Please comment on the audit schema fields and evidence path naming.

Last updated by: Aisha Kapoor (eng-private-deployments)
